Warchanter: Warchanters are bards of the battle line. Where other colleges sing in halls, a Warchanter sings in the mud at the front: drums, horns, and chants that keep a warband moving, fearless, and hitting harder. They fight beside the people they inspire, in mail and with a weapon in hand, and their magic is the rhythm a whole army falls into. Play one if you want to stand in the front rank and make everyone around you better: your war chant (Battle Hymn) starts as a bonus action and boosts every ally's weapon damage, and most of your later features grow stronger while it runs. Your spells come from the Bard's schools of magic, as for any Bard; the college adds to them and takes nothing away.
Plague Doctor: A Plague Doctor is an artificer who studies sickness the way others study gears and gunpowder. They wear beaked masks and leather coats, carry vials of cultured rot, and know that a cure and a poison are often brewed from the same jar. In a fight you coat your weapons in plague, infect enemies, and watch the sickness wear them down turn after turn. Later the infection jumps from host to host, so a single good hit can spread through a whole crowd of foes.
Gravecaller: A Gravecaller is a cleric of a death god who stands at the door between life and death and decides who walks through it. They speak with spirits, comfort the dying, and send restless souls on their way, but they also make sure their friends do not cross over too early. At the table you play a healer who acts at the worst possible moment: when someone falls, you are the one who catches them. Your Channel Divinity can save an ally or drain a foe, so every turn is a quiet choice about who lives and who goes.
Rune Priest: A Rune Priest believes the gods speak in letters, and that holy words carved in the right place can shape the world. They scratch glowing runes onto shields, floors, doorways and the skin of their friends, turning the battlefield into a page of scripture. In combat you mark allies with protective or damaging runes and plant traps that snap shut on charging enemies. You plan ahead, read the fight like a map, and reward the party for standing where you need them.
Storm Caller: A Storm Caller is a druid who hears the voice of nature most clearly in thunder, gales and lightning. Where other druids tend quiet groves, they climb to cliff tops and stand in the rain to feel the sky's anger. In battle you wrap yourself in crackling wind, punish enemies who come close, and blast groups apart with lightning and thunder. You are loud, mobile and dangerous, and you get to fly through the fight on a storm of your own making.
Wilderness Oracle: A Wilderness Oracle is a druid who reads the future in the flight of birds, the bend of grass and the silence of the woods. Villages seek them out for warnings, and they often see trouble coming long before anyone else does. At the table you start each day with two omen rolls you can slip in place of anyone's die, so you decide when a hit lands or a save fails. You are a support player who bends fate itself, and you are almost never caught off guard.
Abyssal Knight: An Abyssal Knight is a fighter who made a deal with demons and now carries their fire in sword and armour. Some seek power for revenge, others for survival, but all of them feel the Abyss pulling at them. In a fight you set your weapon ablaze, soak up hits with the stolen vitality it gives you, and pay back every wound with extra fire. You play a fierce front liner who gets stronger the more blood is spilled, and who scares enemies just by standing there.
Deathblade: A Deathblade is a fighter who treats killing as a craft to be perfected, studying anatomy, weak points and the exact moment a foe will fall. They might be assassins, executioners or simply soldiers who never stopped asking how to do it better. At the table you pick a target, study it, and learn exactly what it fears and what it shrugs off. Your hits land harder against that chosen foe, and later your critical hits and death blows can end a fight in a single swing.
Hex Knight: A Hex Knight is a fighter who swore an oath to a dark power and was given curses in return. They mix sword work with whispered words, marking enemies so that every blow bites deeper. In a fight you hex your chosen target, pile necrotic damage onto it, and weaken one of its abilities so it struggles to escape or resist. As you grow, your hex feeds you, spreads to new targets and finally covers whole groups of foes.
Elemental Fist: An Elemental Fist is a monk who has learned to channel fire, frost, lightning and thunder through their own body. Their training is about balance, letting the elements flow through them without being burned up. In a fight you choose an element for each strike, reach out with a blast of energy, and adapt to whatever your enemies are weak against. Later you can explode with elemental bursts and finally wrap yourself in the element as a living avatar.
Iron Fist: An Iron Fist is a monk who has hardened their body through brutal training until flesh and bone feel like forged metal. Their schools teach endurance first and striking second, often in temples built around a forge. At the table you are a sturdy monk who shrugs off blows, hits harder than other monks, and knocks foes flat. You stand in the front line where most monks would dance away, and you are very hard to put down.
Sand Dancer: A Sand Dancer is a monk from desert traditions who fights with dust, wind and confusion as much as with fists. They move like a sandstorm, always shifting, never where the enemy expects. In combat you blind foes with kicked-up sand, slip away behind drifting dust, and turn the ground into a trap that trips enemies. You are a slippery controller who makes the battlefield hard for everyone but you.
Oathbreaker Knight: An Oathbreaker Knight is a paladin who broke their sacred vow and discovered that the act of betrayal itself holds power. They are often hunted by their old order, and they walk a hard road between redemption and something darker. At the table you are a cunning paladin who strikes from trust and surprise, dealing heavy necrotic damage to foes who never saw it coming. Your aura weakens enemy courage, and the broken pieces of your old oath protect you when you are hurt.
Thornwalker: A Thornwalker is a ranger who has bonded with the sharp, dangerous side of the wild: brambles, briars and thorned vines. They guard forests by making them painful to enter, and some have thorns growing from their own skin. In a fight you sprout spikes that hurt anyone who strikes you and add sting to your own attacks. Later you bind enemies in vines and carpet the ground with thorns, turning the battlefield into a garden that fights for you.
Blood Dancer: A Blood Dancer is a rogue who turns their own blood into a weapon, spending health for speed and deadly strikes. They are often outcasts or members of secret cults that believe pain is the purest form of power. At the table you choose when to bleed: losing a few hit points lets you hit harder or dart across the battlefield. It is a risky, exciting style where you gamble your health for big moments, then claw it back when foes fall.
Chaos Shaper: A Chaos Shaper is a sorcerer born with wild, unstable magic who has learned to steer it rather than fear it. They still never know exactly what will happen, but they can nudge the dice in their favour. In play you add small random bonuses to your spells, force rerolls on important rolls, and gamble for bigger damage. It is a lively, unpredictable style for players who enjoy luck, risk and a little bit of mischief.
Dragonblood: A Dragonblood sorcerer carries the blood of a dragon ancestor, and that power shows itself in scales, pride and elemental magic. Their families may be noble houses, ancient cults or simple folk with one strange grandparent. At the table you are tougher than most sorcerers, with extra hit points and natural armour, and you hit harder with spells of your ancestor's element. Later you grow wings and an aura of dread, becoming a small dragon in all but shape.
Gnome Bloodline: A Gnome Bloodline sorcerer draws power from Gnome, the dead spirit of Earth, whose strength still sleeps in stone and soil. They feel every footstep through the ground and often seem calm, stubborn and slow to anger. In a fight you sense hidden enemies through tremors, add crushing force to your spells, and harden your skin against blows. You are a sturdy, grounded caster who is very hard to move, knock down or surprise.
Ignis Bloodline: An Ignis Bloodline sorcerer carries a spark of Ignis, the dead spirit of Fire, and that spark burns hot in everything they do. They are often passionate and restless, and they feel cold far less than others. At the table you are a pure fire caster who adds extra damage to flame spells and cannot be hurt by your own blasts. Later your fire ignores resistance and leaps from one fallen foe to the next.
Mirror Mage: A Mirror Mage is a sorcerer whose magic copies and reflects, as if every spell they touch becomes a looking glass. Some were born under strange moons, others were touched by enchanted mirrors as children. In a fight you turn aside attacks with shimmering wards, copy single-target spells onto a second foe, and bounce enemy spells back at their casters. You are a clever, reactive caster who loves turning an enemy's best move against them.
Sylph Bloodline: A Sylph Bloodline sorcerer carries the breath of Sylph, the dead spirit of Air, and the wind seems to follow them wherever they go. They are light on their feet, hard to pin down and often a little carefree. In a fight you push enemies around with every damaging spell, change your gifts each day with the four winds, and later fly freely above the battle. You are a mobile controller who decides where everyone on the field ends up.
Undine Bloodline: An Undine Bloodline sorcerer carries the tide of Undine, the dead spirit of Water, and is as much at home in the sea as on land. They tend to be patient and caring, but their power can turn to crushing waves when needed. At the table you heal a friend every time you cast a real spell, armour yourself in frost, and sweep foes around with currents. You play a caster who keeps the party standing while still hitting hard when it counts.
Diamond's Patron: A warlock bound to Diamond's Patron draws power from the shattered remains of Diamond, whose broken shards still hold a cold and brilliant will. Pieces of that shard live under your skin, and in the right light you glitter. At the table you are a hard-to-kill warlock who can turn a deadly hit into nothing and blind enemies with flashes of light. Later your eldritch blasts refract through you, splashing radiant damage onto a second foe.
Iron's Patron: A warlock bound to Iron's Patron serves Iron himself, a mighty being sealed away but not dead, who lends his strength through chains and steel. Followers are often smiths, soldiers or prisoners who heard his voice in the dark. At the table you are a tough, weapon-ready warlock who can reshape your blade for defence or damage. As you grow, you shrug off death, bind enemies in spectral chains and hammer them with iron-hard eldritch blasts.
Void Caller: A Void Caller is a warlock whose patron lives in the empty space between the planes, a place of total nothingness. Their magic feels cold and hollow, and they often speak of silence as if it were a friend. In a fight you open pockets of void on your foes, adding force damage to your spells and stopping them from healing fully. Later you blink through nothing, unmake enemy spells and swallow a foe whole for a moment before spitting it back out.
Astromancer: An Astromancer is a wizard who studies the stars and the deep dark between them, drawing magic from distant suns and falling comets. They keep detailed star charts and believe the heavens hold answers to every question. At the table you boost your spells with a choice of stars, adding radiant damage, healing a friend or steadying your concentration. Later you call down falling stars, shield allies with an orbiting light and crush enemies under the weight of stellar gravity.
Aether Engineer: Aether Engineers are inventors who stopped trusting the ground. They build humming rigs of brass and crystal that catch the invisible aether in the air and turn it into lift. In play you keep your party mobile, floating over pits, walls, and danger while your stored charge feeds extra tricks. You shine in vertical fights and in any place where others are stuck below.
Blood Titan: Blood Titans are warriors who feed their own blood to an old giant spirit in exchange for its strength. Every wound makes them bigger, harder, and angrier. At the table you dive into the front line and let enemies hit you, because the more you bleed the tougher you become. You trade careful defense for raw size and staying power.
Path of the World Tree: Barbarians of the World Tree feel the great cosmic tree whose roots and branches link every realm. Their rage flows like sap through that tree, healing friends and reaching across distance. In combat you protect allies with bursts of vitality, drag enemies close, and step along the branches to cross the battlefield. You play a tough front liner who also keeps the whole group standing.
College of Dance: Bards of the College of Dance tell their stories with their whole bodies. Every spin, step, and leap is part of a performance, and a fight is just another stage. You fight unarmored with swift, graceful strikes while your movement lifts and guides your allies. You play a nimble skirmisher who keeps the whole party light on its feet.
College of Lore: Bards of the College of Lore gather stories, secrets, and spells from every corner of the world. They value knowing things over winning brawls, and they trade rumors in taverns and libraries alike. At the table you cover many skills, cut enemy rolls down with sharp words, and pull useful spells from other classes. You play the clever helper who always has the right answer or the right spell.
Grave Domain: Grave Domain clerics serve the gods who guard the line between life and death. They see death as a natural end and fight hard against undead who break that rule. At the table you keep dying allies alive with strong healing, punish foes with curses that make them vulnerable, and turn deadly blows into ordinary ones. You play a careful guardian who decides who walks away from the edge.
Circle of Stars: Druids of the Circle of Stars read the night sky and draw power from its constellations. They carry a star map and believe the stars hold the stories of the world. In play you use Wild Shape to take a glowing starry form as an archer, a healer, or a steady dragon. Your daily omens let you nudge rolls for friends or against foes.
Circle of the Sea: Druids of the Circle of the Sea carry the ocean's fury wherever they go, even far inland. Salt spray, cold waves, and storm winds answer their call. At the table you spend Wild Shape to wrap yourself in a crashing aura that chills and shoves enemies. Later you swim, fly on storm winds, and share that aura with an ally.
Iron Vanguard: Iron Vanguards are soldiers trained to be the wall that never breaks. They wear the heaviest armor they can find and plant their feet so their friends can fight behind them. At the table you stand still, soak blows, and step in front of attacks aimed at allies. You play the anchor of the battle line, not the one who chases enemies down.
Way of Ruin: Monks of the Way of Ruin study how things break instead of how they flow. They strike at cracks in armor, bone, and will until everything gives way. At the table you weaken a foe's defenses with each blow, then land crushing strikes when it is already hurt. You play a focused finisher who tears down the toughest enemies.
Oath of Ash: Paladins of the Oath of Ash swear that evil will burn until nothing is left. They do not offer mercy, and the cinders they leave behind are a warning to anyone who would follow the same path. At the table you smite with fire that lingers, scorch enemies who stay close, and keep burning even as you fall. You play a fierce front liner who punishes anyone in reach.
Oath of Silence: Paladins of the Oath of Silence serve a justice that is never announced. They move quietly, strike without warning, and leave no sound behind. At the table you sneak in armor, slip past enemies with silent smites, and shut down spellcasters with zones of silence. You play a holy hunter who strikes before the guilty know you are there.
Moon Hunter: Moon Hunters are rangers who follow old traditions of hunting werewolves and other shapechangers. They work best under the moon, when their senses sharpen and their arrows fly true. At the table you scout at night, mark a target, and punish creatures that hide behind a false shape. You play a patient tracker who becomes deadly when the moon is up.
Shade Walker: Shade Walkers are rogues who treat shadows as a hidden city with its own streets and doors. They slip from one dark patch to the next and never leave a trail. At the table you hide easily, take shortcuts through shadow, and vanish when hurt. You play a scout and infiltrator who goes where no one else can follow.
Celestial Ruin: Celestial Ruin sorcerers carry the blood of a star that fell from the sky long ago. Its light still lives in them, but it comes down hard and late, like a meteor. At the table you mark targets and call down delayed bursts of radiant power that punish foes who stay put. You play a heavy hitter who plans a turn ahead.
Wild Magic (Sorcerer): Wild Magic sorcerers carry raw chaos in their blood instead of a clean family gift. Their power might come from a strange accident, a magical storm, or nothing anyone can name. At the table your spells can spark surprising surges that help or hurt, and you can bend luck for friends and foes. You play a bold, unpredictable caster who makes every fight memorable.
The Hollow King: The Hollow King is an empty crown resting on an empty throne, a patron with no face and no voice. Warlocks who serve it borrow the weight of a rule that no one truly holds. At the table you make enemies hesitate, draw strength when allies fall, and force whole groups to kneel. You play a commanding presence who controls the field through fear and borrowed authority.
Rune Sage: Rune Sages are wizards who study runes as a slower, steadier second spellbook. They carve marks into stone, steel, and skin that hold magic until it is needed. At the table you prepare small runic boosts and wards ahead of time, then cash them in to recover spell slots or unleash one great glyph. You play a patient planner who wins by being ready.
Runesmith: Runesmiths are artificers who carve power into the surface of things instead of building machines. They travel with chisels, ink, and a satchel of half-finished sigils, and they can turn a plain sword or a dented shield into something special for a while. At the table you are the party's support crafter, handing out temporary boosts to everyone's gear before and during a fight. As you level, your runes last longer, cover more items, and finally grant one truly impressive magical property.
Path of Ruin: Barbarians of the Path of Ruin do not just fight their enemies. They tear down the walls, floors, and pillars around them too. Many come from raider clans or siege crews who learned that a broken battlefield favours the one who broke it. In play you smash cover, knock foes off their feet, and leave rough ground behind that only you can cross freely. You shine in tight fights where the room itself can become a weapon.
Storm Reaver: Storm Reavers are barbarians whose fury calls the sky down with them. Thunder rolls when they roar, and sparks jump from their weapons into anyone standing too close. Some were struck by lightning and lived, while others made a pact with a storm spirit on a high peak. At the table you are a fast, hard-hitting front liner who spreads damage to more than one enemy and later deafens and blasts whole groups.
College of Dreams: Bards of the College of Dreams sing the soft songs that come before sleep and the strange ones that come after it. They learn their craft in quiet halls where students practise lullabies and record the dreams of their teachers. In play you slow enemies down with drowsiness, slip into sleeping minds to learn secrets, and haunt foes with nightmares. Late in your career you can bend reality just enough to tip a whole fight in your party's favour.
Astral Domain: Clerics of the Astral Domain draw their power from the stars themselves rather than from one god's voice. They read omens in the night sky and believe the heavens hold the world together with invisible threads. In play you protect allies with shields of starlight, drag enemies together with gravity, and step partly out of the world to avoid harm. At the highest levels you become a being of starlight who flies above the battle, healing friends and burning foes.
Life Domain: The Life Domain is the heart of healing magic. Its clerics serve gods of health, mercy, and renewal, and they see every saved life as an act of worship. Every healing spell you cast restores more than usual, and you mend yourself as you mend others. At the table you are the party's anchor, wearing heavy armour on the front line and making sure nobody stays down for long.
Circle of the Eclipse: Druids of the Circle of the Eclipse honour the moment when light and shadow meet in the sky. They hold that neither day nor night is good or evil, only that both must stay in balance. In play you shift between a light stance and a dark stance, changing what your Wild Shape and your magic bring to the fight. You can slip through shadow, add radiant or necrotic power to your beast forms, and later blind every enemy around you with a sudden eclipse.
Ashen Commander: Ashen Commanders are fighters who lead from the middle of the fire. Their banners are scorched, their armour is stained with soot, and they have survived battles that burned everything else around them. In play you steady your allies against fear, set the ground under you alight, and spend your own reactions to keep your friends fighting. At the peak of your career you refuse to let anyone near you fall, and your fallen comrades rise again in a burst of flame.
Void Knight: Void Knights are fighters who were marked by the Void, the empty dark beyond the Mortal Realm. No order trains them, and most learned their strange gifts after surviving something that should have erased them. In play you blink across the battlefield, strike through armour and magical defences, and pull enemy lines out of shape. You are a mobile warrior who closes distance in an instant and is very hard to pin down or finish off.
Way of the Empty Palm: Monks of the Way of the Empty Palm train to hold onto nothing, not weapons, not possessions, and not fear. Their teachers say that a hand that grasps can be seized, but an open hand can never be taken. In play you strip weapons from your enemies, slip out of every hold, and learn to resist the kind of harm you have just seen. You are a slippery duelist who frustrates grapplers and armed foes alike.
Oath of Devotion: Paladins of the Oath of Devotion follow the oldest ideals of knighthood. They swear to be honest, brave, kind, and to stand between the weak and those who would harm them. In play you bless your weapon with holy light, drive back fiends and undead, and protect nearby allies from being charmed. At the height of your power you shine like the sun itself and burn the wicked who stand near you.
Beast Lord: Beast Lords are rangers who run with a pack instead of a single loyal animal. They speak the language of growls and gestures, and their two bonded beasts follow their lead like hunting dogs following an alpha. In play you control two companions, setting up flanks and focused attacks on the same target. As you grow, your pack grows tougher and you can call even more beasts to join a fight for a short time.
Void Stalker: Void Stalkers are rangers who hunt the creatures that slip into the Mortal Realm from the Void. Their prey can be invisible, half real, or able to walk through walls, so they train their eyes to see what others cannot. In play you track and strike unseen enemies, fire arrows that ignore protective magic, and step through space to keep up with your quarry. You finish hunts with a single precise shot that erases badly wounded foes.
Soul Thief: Soul Thieves are rogues who steal more than coins. Through secret rites passed between criminal circles, they learn to take life force, memories, and talents from the people they strike. In play you drain a little health with your sneak attacks, borrow tricks from defeated foes, and weaken a marked target against your blows. At the peak of the craft you can rip away a large share of an enemy's life or power in one daring theft.
Draconic Bloodline: Draconic Bloodline sorcerers carry the blood of a dragon somewhere in their family line. That ancient heritage hardens their skin like scales and fills their magic with the element of their dragon ancestor. In play you are tougher than most spellcasters and deal extra damage with spells of your chosen element. Later you sprout dragon wings to fly and can fill your enemies with awe or terror just by being present.
The Ashen Eye: The Ashen Eye is a patron that is little more than a burnt-out watcher, a great eye that sees through smoke from a world that already burned. It asks little of its warlocks beyond that they keep looking and remember what they see. In play you see clearly through smoke and fog, leave burning embers on foes hit by your eldritch blast, and sense danger a moment before it strikes. At higher levels you can briefly see everything around you, even through solid walls.
The Star Eater: The Star Eater is a hungry patron that swallows light and feeds on things that are already dying. Its warlocks share in that hunger and grow stronger whenever a wounded foe falls. In play you finish off injured enemies with your eldritch blast to heal yourself, shrug off radiant damage, and steal powers from strong foes you defeat. Late in your career you unleash bursts of devouring darkness that hurt enemies and restore your own strength.
School of Evocation: Wizards of the School of Evocation study raw destructive magic like fire, lightning, cold, and force. They are the artillery of any adventuring party, and they learn to shape their blasts so friends stay safe inside the blaze. In play you drop large area spells without fear of hurting allies, and even your cantrips still hurt enemies who dodge them. At the highest levels you can push a spell to its absolute maximum power, though doing so too often harms you.
Soul Mechanist: Soul Mechanists are artificers who believe a machine is only half alive until something inside it can want. Instead of springs and gears alone, they trap small wisps of spirit in brass shells and give them a body to serve in. Your bound spirit fights at your side, slips into nearby objects, and burns your own life force for extra power when you need it. At the table you play a crafter who blends constructs with a touch of the eerie, trading hit points for flexibility.
Path of the Berserker: Berserkers are warriors who stop holding anything back once the fighting starts. They come from raider bands, pit fights, and frontier towns where the loudest and fiercest survive. You rage, frenzy, and swing again and again, ignoring fear and charm while your fury lasts. The cost comes later, when exhaustion catches up with a body pushed far past its limits.
College of Ash: Bards of the College of Ash sing over graves and battlefields, giving the dead a proper farewell and the living a reason to keep going. They are hired for funerals, called to the sites of disasters, and sometimes feared as omens of death. Your dirges shake the resolve of foes while your songs of memory steady your companions. In play you are a support bard who weakens enemies, shields allies from fire, and turns grief into strength.
College of Echoing Chants: Bards of the College of Echoing Chants learn their craft in great stone halls where every sound returns many times. They teach that a spell, like a note, does not have to end when it is first spoken. You repeat your magic onto second targets, stretch your performances longer, and eventually fill a whole battlefield with your chorus. You play a bard who gets extra value out of every spell and keeps the party supported over long fights.
Flame Domain: Clerics of the Flame Domain worship fire itself as a holy force that cleans, warms, and destroys. Some serve temples of hearth and forge, while others wander as zealots who see every wildfire as a sermon. You wrap your strikes in flame, guard your allies against burning, and call down spreading fires on your enemies. At the table you are a front line priest who mixes healing and burning in the same breath.
Circle of Rot: Druids of the Circle of Rot honor decay as the half of nature that others forget. They tend fungus groves, swamps, and fallen forests, believing nothing can grow until something else breaks down. You sicken enemies with a touch, choke them with spore clouds, and take on blighted animal forms. In play you are a druid who wears foes down over time while quietly keeping your allies standing.
Circle of the Land: Druids of the Circle of the Land are bound to one kind of terrain, such as frozen tundra, deep forest, or lightless caverns. They often serve as keepers of ancient stone circles and sacred groves, carrying the lore of their home wherever they go. You gain extra spells shaped by your chosen land, recover magic during short rests, and move freely through wild places. At the table you are a spellcasting druid with a wide toolkit, more focused on magic than on Wild Shape.
Champion: Champions are fighters who have trained their bodies to the very peak of what a mortal can do. They need no magic or clever tricks, only strength, speed, and stubborn grit. You land critical hits more often, gain extra fighting styles, and eventually heal yourself just by refusing to fall. In play you are a simple, reliable warrior who is easy to run and dangerous in every fight.
Way of Echoes: Monks of the Way of Echoes train until their movements leave traces behind them in the air. Their masters teach that every action ripples outward, and a skilled monk can catch that ripple and make it strike. You leave afterimages that soak up blows, land doubled strikes, and in time fight beside a whole crowd of your own echoes. At the table you are a slippery, high tempo monk who is hard to pin down and hits more often than it seems possible.
Way of the Open Hand: Monks of the Way of the Open Hand are masters of pure unarmed combat. They study in mountain monasteries and teach that the body itself is the finest weapon. You knock foes down, push them away, and stop them from reacting with every Flurry of Blows, heal your own wounds, and eventually learn a strike that can kill with a touch. In play you are a mobile skirmisher who controls the battlefield with your fists.
Oath of Eternity: Paladins of the Oath of Eternity swear to endure, to be the last one standing when every other defender has fallen. Their order guards ancient vaults, sacred borders, and long promises that must outlast kingdoms. You shrug off fear and charm, shake off exhaustion, and refuse even death itself for a little while longer. At the table you are a tough, patient defender who holds the line so the rest of the party can win.
Hunter: Hunters are rangers who guard the edges of the civilized world against the monsters that prowl beyond it. They learn to fight giants, hordes, and lone killers alike, choosing the right answer for each threat. You pick tactics that deal extra damage, defend against swarms, and strike many foes at once. In play you are a flexible combat ranger who adapts to whatever the wilds throw at you.
Nightblade: Nightblades are rogues who treat darkness as a road rather than a hiding place. They often serve secret orders, rival noble houses, or temples of night that need someone to vanish and reappear behind a target. You step from shadow to shadow, silence foes with a strike, and turn invisible in dim light. At the table you are a mobile assassin who picks a target, slips behind it, and is gone before anyone can respond.
Thief: Thieves are rogues who make their living by getting into places they should not be and leaving with things they should not have. They are burglars, smugglers, treasure hunters, and dungeon delvers. You use items quickly, climb and jump with ease, stay hidden as you move, and can use almost any magic item you find. In play you are the party's expert at locks, traps, and strange devices, and you strike first when combat begins.
Voidborn: Voidborn sorcerers were touched by the empty space between worlds before they were even born. Their magic does not come from a dragon, a god, or a storm, but from an absence that hums quietly inside them. You resist force damage, cut through defenses, step briefly out of the world, and silence other spells before they finish. At the table you are a strange and slippery caster who shuts down enemy magic as well as you deal damage.
The Fiend (Patron): Warlocks of the Fiend have made a deal with a devil, a demon, or another power from the lower planes. Such patrons offer strength and survival in exchange for souls, service, or slow corruption. You grow tougher each time you defeat a foe, bend luck in your favor, resist the attacks that threaten you most, and finally cast enemies into hell itself. In play you are a hard hitting fire caster who stays in the fight longer than most warlocks.
Chronomancer: Chronomancers are wizards who study the small seams between moments rather than trying to rule time as a whole. Their schools are full of clocks, sand glasses, and journals that record the same minute over and over. You borrow extra reactions, slow your enemies, reuse spells you have already cast, and eventually act twice in a single round. At the table you are a clever support wizard who always seems to have one more move ready.
Void Scholar: Void Scholars are wizards who treat the Void as a field of careful study, not a source of raw power to grab. They fill libraries with maps of empty space and theories about why magic unravels at its edges. You identify strange magic, shrug off force damage, fold space to move, and strip magical effects from your enemies.
